title: U.S. House · Florida's 7th District
area: East-central Florida, including parts of Volusia, Seminole and Orange counties.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Cory Mills did not win the August 18, 2026 Republican primary, which Ryan Elijah won over Michael Johnson and Sarah Ulrich. Bale Dalton won the Democratic primary over Alan Grayson and Marialana Kinter. Christopher Dennison (Libertarian) also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Ryan Elijah
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary over incumbent Cory Mills, Michael Johnson and Sarah Ulrich.

priorities.text: Lowering taxes and cutting wasteful government spending and fraud.
Reducing healthcare regulation to lower costs and premiums.
Supporting law enforcement, including federal funding for training and technology and tougher penalties for assaulting officers.

positions.summary: Says he will push for federal funding for law-enforcement training, technology and personnel, and support tougher penalties for assaulting or shooting officers.
positions.quote: Federal funding for training, new technology and personnel are critical for the safety of our community.

positions.summary: His campaign issues page says he strongly supports the Save America Act, which he describes as ensuring only American citizens can vote.
positions.quote: He strongly supports the Save America Act, which ensures only American citizens can vote in our elections — because citizenship must matter.

statements.quote: Ryan is pro-life and believes every life is a sacred gift from God.
He is a staunch supporter of the Second Amendment and has earned an “A” rating with the NRA.
We must continue to secure our borders and oppose any measures that weaken enforcement or prioritize non-citizens over American safety.
That’s why he champions parental rights and school choice, empowering families to make the best decisions for their kids and have transparency on curriculum.
He also believes healthcare costs can be reduced by providing individuals with tax benefits, such as expanded Health Savings Accounts.

candidates.name: Bale Dalton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Alan Grayson and Marialana Kinter.

priorities.text: Says his top priority is making Florida affordable again, addressing gas, health care, housing and insurance costs.
Wants to make it illegal for members of Congress to trade stocks in companies they regulate.
Wants to restore Medicaid and Medicare funding and reverse premium increases, and supports negotiating prescription drug prices.

positions.summary: His campaign priorities page calls for restoring Medicaid funding, reversing health care premium increases, and building on the Affordable Care Act.
positions.quote: We need to elect members of Congress who will restore funding to Medicaid, reverse premium cuts, and protect Social Security and Medicare for generations to come.

positions.summary: His campaign priorities page calls for reversing tariffs that he says raise costs for families and small businesses.
positions.quote: We need to stop the bleeding, by reversing health care premium hikes and illegal, unpredictable tariffs.

positions.summary: His campaign priorities page says he supports codifying Roe into federal law.
positions.quote: That’s why I support codifying Roe into federal law, to put these decisions back where they belong – with patients.

positions.summary: His campaign priorities page says he supports raising the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: With prices rising, wages also need to keep up – which is why I support raising the federal minimum wage and passing the PRO Act, so labor unions can advocate for workers in a changing economy.

candidates.name: Christopher Dennison
candidates.ballotNote: Libertarian primary was canceled; advanced unopposed.
candidates.researchNotes: Checked Christopher Dennison's own Ballotpedia page (https://ballotpedia.org/Christopher_Dennison, no completed 2026 Candidate Connection survey, no campaign website listed) and a web search; a Seminole County Chamber candidate forum report (mynews13.com, August 2026) notes only that Dennison did not attend. No campaign website, biography, or policy statements were found.

researchNotes: Open seat after incumbent Cory Mills lost his primary; Dalton's survey references an ongoing House Ethics Committee investigation into Mills, which is not independently verified here since Mills is not on the November ballot. No campaign website, questionnaire or public statements by Christopher Dennison were found, so no positions are listed for him. Ryan Elijah's statements are from his campaign issues page. Biography gaps: no campaign website, news coverage or candidate survey found for Christopher Dennison; Elijah's birthplace and employer history beyond FOX 35 Orlando are not covered in the sources loaded.
